questions.q: In the CSA shared responsibility model, which party is always responsible for classifying and protecting the data placed in a cloud service?
choices: The cloud provider
The CSA STAR registry
The underlying IaaS hypervisor vendor
The cloud customer
questions.why: Data ownership, classification, and governance always remain the customer's responsibility across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS.

questions.q: What does the CSA Cloud Controls Matrix (CCM) primarily provide?
choices: A contractual SLA template for negotiating with providers
A live vulnerability scanner for cloud workloads
A penetration testing methodology for containers
A cloud-specific control framework mapped to other standards and regulations
questions.why: The CCM is a cybersecurity control framework for cloud computing, with mappings to standards like ISO 27001, NIST, and PCI DSS.

questions.q: The Consensus Assessments Initiative Questionnaire (CAIQ) is best described as what?
choices: A set of yes/no questions letting customers assess a provider's security against the CCM
A binding audit report signed by an accredited third party
A cloud incident notification standard
A runtime configuration baseline enforced by the provider
questions.why: The CAIQ offers standardized questions aligned to CCM controls so customers can document provider security posture.

questions.q: The CSA STAR registry Level 1 is based on what type of assessment?
choices: Provider self-assessment using CAIQ or CCM
Continuous automated monitoring by CSA
A third-party audit against SOC 2
A government-issued FedRAMP authorization
questions.why: STAR Level 1 is a self-assessment where providers publish a completed CAIQ or CCM; higher levels add third-party attestation.

questions.q: Which cloud service model gives the customer the most responsibility for securing the operating system and applications?
choices: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
Software as a Service (SaaS)
Function as a Service managed entirely by the provider
Platform as a Service (PaaS)
questions.why: In IaaS the provider secures the physical and virtualization layers while the customer manages OS, runtime, and apps.

questions.q: According to CSA guidance, what is the essential characteristic that most distinguishes cloud from traditional hosting?
choices: The use of virtual machines instead of physical servers
Broad network access, resource pooling, and on-demand self-service
A fixed monthly billing contract
Mandatory encryption of all data at rest
questions.why: NIST and CSA define cloud by essential characteristics including on-demand self-service, resource pooling, and rapid elasticity.

questions.q: In cloud data security, what is the primary benefit of the customer holding the encryption keys rather than the provider?
choices: It removes the need to encrypt data in transit
It shifts breach liability entirely to the provider
It preserves customer control and can prevent provider access to plaintext
It automatically satisfies all compliance requirements
questions.why: Customer-managed keys, including BYOK and HYOK models, let the customer control access and limit provider visibility into plaintext.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a cloud access security broker (CASB)?
choices: To provide visibility and policy enforcement between users and cloud services
To act as the primary key management server for the provider
To generate STAR registry attestations automatically
To replace the provider's hypervisor security controls
questions.why: CASBs sit between users and cloud services to enforce security policy, discover shadow IT, and give usage visibility.

questions.q: Under ENISA cloud risk guidance, which is identified as a top risk unique to the cloud outsourcing model?
choices: Paper document mishandling
Local power outages at the customer office
Loss of governance over data and operations
Physical theft of employee laptops
questions.why: ENISA highlights loss of governance as a top cloud risk because the customer cedes some control to the provider.

questions.q: What does vendor lock-in risk in cloud primarily threaten?
choices: The customer's ability to migrate data and workloads to another provider
The accuracy of the CCM control mappings
The provider's uptime SLA guarantees
The encryption strength of data at rest
questions.why: Lock-in stems from proprietary formats and APIs that make portability and migration difficult, an ENISA and CSA-cited risk.

questions.q: In CSA guidance, what is the recommended first step when moving a workload to the cloud?
choices: Identify the asset and evaluate its sensitivity and required controls
Encrypt every field with a unique key
Purchase a STAR Level 2 attestation
Select the cheapest provider available
questions.why: CSA's process starts by identifying the asset and its value, then mapping it to potential deployment and service models.

questions.q: Which IAM concept is most critical when federating identities into a cloud provider?
choices: Sharing a single root account across teams
Disabling multi-factor authentication for automation accounts
Storing all user passwords in the provider's database
Establishing trust and secure token exchange between identity provider and relying party
questions.why: Federation relies on a trusted identity provider issuing assertions or tokens that the cloud service consumes as the relying party.

questions.q: What is the principle of least privilege as applied to cloud entitlements?
choices: Give every service account full API access by default
Grant identities only the permissions required to perform their tasks
Grant all users administrator rights to reduce support tickets
Rotate keys only when a breach is confirmed
questions.why: Least privilege limits each identity to the minimum entitlements needed, reducing blast radius in cloud environments.

questions.q: In cloud incident response, why is provider cooperation and contractual clarity important?
choices: Encryption makes customer-side response unnecessary
The provider is legally required to handle all customer incidents
The customer often lacks direct access to underlying logs and forensic data
The CCM prohibits customers from investigating incidents
questions.why: Customers depend on providers for lower-layer telemetry and forensics, so response roles must be defined in the contract or SLA.

questions.q: What is a key challenge for digital forensics in multi-tenant cloud environments?
choices: The impossibility of encrypting evidence
The absence of any logging capability in cloud
The requirement to physically seize the provider's servers
Isolating one tenant's data without exposing other tenants' data
questions.why: Multi-tenancy complicates evidence collection because resources are shared and one tenant's forensics must not compromise others.

questions.q: Which practice best supports secure application development in cloud (DevSecOps)?
choices: Relying solely on the provider to patch application code
Integrating automated security testing into the CI/CD pipeline
Deferring all security testing until after production release
Disabling logging to improve deployment speed
questions.why: Embedding security testing into CI/CD pipelines shifts security left and matches CSA application security guidance.

questions.q: What does the term 'management plane' refer to in cloud security?
choices: The interfaces and APIs used to configure and control cloud resources
The physical network cabling in the data center
The customer's on-premises firewall cluster
The billing dashboard only
questions.why: The management plane is the control interface for provisioning and managing resources, and compromising it can affect the whole account.

questions.q: Why is securing the cloud management plane considered especially critical?
choices: It is not accessible over the network
It is fully managed by the customer's ISP
Its compromise can grant broad control over all hosted resources
It is the only component that stores encryption keys
questions.why: The management plane's broad reach means a compromise can affect every workload, so strong access control and MFA are essential.

questions.q: What is 'tokenization' as a data protection technique in cloud?
choices: Hashing passwords with a salt
Encrypting data with a rotating symmetric key
Splitting a file across multiple regions
Replacing sensitive data with non-sensitive substitute values
questions.why: Tokenization swaps sensitive values for tokens with no exploitable meaning, often to reduce compliance scope like PCI DSS.

questions.q: In the CSA data security lifecycle, which phase focuses on removing data no longer needed?
choices: Share
Store
Create
Destroy
questions.why: The CSA data security lifecycle phases are create, store, use, share, archive, and destroy; destroy handles secure disposal.

questions.q: What is a primary concern when a cloud provider subcontracts services to a fourth party?
choices: Guaranteed compliance with all regulations
Elimination of the shared responsibility model
Automatic improvement of the provider's SLA
Extended supply chain risk and reduced transparency over data handling
questions.why: Nested subcontracting lengthens the supply chain, so customers must understand fourth-party dependencies and their controls.

questions.q: Why does CSA recommend reviewing a provider's SOC 2 or ISO 27001 attestations alongside the CAIQ?
choices: They automatically encrypt customer data
They are required to access the management plane
They replace the need for any contractual agreement
They provide independent third-party validation of controls the CAIQ self-reports
questions.why: Independent audit reports corroborate the self-reported CAIQ, giving stronger assurance of the provider's control environment.

questions.q: What is the security implication of cloud 'elasticity' and auto-scaling?
choices: Security controls become unnecessary at scale
New instances must inherit hardened, consistent security configurations automatically
Auto-scaling disables all logging
Elasticity prevents any misconfiguration from spreading
questions.why: Rapid scaling means insecure images or misconfigurations propagate quickly, so baselines and automation must enforce hardening.

questions.q: In the context of cloud, what does 'data residency' concern?
choices: The retention period before deletion
The encryption algorithm used at rest
The number of replicas kept for redundancy
The geographic location where data is stored and processed
questions.why: Data residency addresses legal and regulatory requirements about where data physically resides across provider regions.

questions.q: What is a virtual private cloud (VPC) primarily used for?
choices: Logically isolating a customer's network resources within a public cloud
Providing a dedicated physical data center to one customer
Managing the provider's billing
Encrypting all data at the application layer
questions.why: A VPC gives logically isolated networking with customer-controlled subnets, routing, and segmentation inside shared infrastructure.

questions.q: Why is microsegmentation valuable in cloud network security?
choices: It removes the need to patch operating systems
It limits lateral movement by enforcing granular traffic policies between workloads
It guarantees zero downtime
It eliminates the need for identity management
questions.why: Microsegmentation applies fine-grained policies so a compromised workload cannot freely move laterally to others.

questions.q: According to CSA, what is the risk of relying only on a provider's default configurations?
choices: Defaults may prioritize usability over security, leaving gaps the customer must close
Defaults are always fully compliant with every regulation
Defaults automatically enable customer-managed keys
Defaults transfer all responsibility to the provider
questions.why: Provider defaults often favor ease of use, so customers must review and harden configurations to meet their requirements.

questions.q: What is the main goal of Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) tooling?
choices: Encrypting all data in transit
Replacing the provider's physical security
Issuing STAR attestations
Continuously detecting misconfigurations and compliance drift across cloud accounts
questions.why: CSPM continuously assesses cloud configurations against benchmarks and policies to catch misconfigurations and drift.

questions.q: In cloud governance, what should a cloud security policy be aligned to first?
choices: The cheapest available service tier
The provider's marketing recommendations
The most restrictive setting regardless of impact
The organization's overall risk tolerance and business objectives
questions.why: Governance must flow from enterprise risk appetite and business goals so cloud controls support rather than hinder the mission.

questions.q: What does 'crypto-shredding' accomplish for cloud data disposal?
choices: Physically degaussing the provider's drives
Compressing data before deletion
Rendering data unrecoverable by destroying the encryption keys
Overwriting physical disk sectors seven times
questions.why: When customers cannot physically wipe shared media, deleting the keys makes the ciphertext permanently unreadable.

questions.q: Why are hardware security modules (HSMs) used in cloud key management?
choices: They provide tamper-resistant generation and storage of cryptographic keys
They accelerate network throughput for all traffic
They replace the need for IAM policies
They store application source code securely
questions.why: HSMs protect keys in tamper-resistant hardware, and cloud HSM services let customers meet strong key protection requirements.

questions.q: What is the significance of API security in cloud environments?
choices: APIs are only used for billing and pose little risk
API security is entirely the provider's responsibility
APIs cannot be authenticated in cloud
APIs are the primary interface to cloud resources, so weak API security exposes the whole environment
questions.why: Cloud is API-driven; insecure keys, tokens, or endpoints can expose management and data planes to attackers.

questions.q: In the CSA guidance, what is 'immutable infrastructure'?
choices: Infrastructure that can never be deleted
Infrastructure that is replaced rather than modified in place when changes are needed
Storage that cannot be encrypted
Servers that block all inbound traffic permanently
questions.why: Immutable infrastructure redeploys new hardened instances instead of patching running ones, improving consistency and auditability.

questions.q: Which factor most increases the difficulty of compliance auditing in cloud?
choices: Mandatory on-site inspection of all providers
The absence of any logging in cloud services
The prohibition of third-party audits
Limited customer visibility into provider-controlled layers
questions.why: Customers cannot directly audit provider-managed layers, so they rely on attestations, the STAR registry, and contractual reporting.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) plan for cloud workloads?
choices: To transfer all recovery duties to the customer's ISP
To eliminate the need for backups
To replace the shared responsibility model
To maintain and restore operations across regions or providers during disruptions
questions.why: BC/DR planning uses multi-region or multi-provider strategies and tested backups to meet recovery objectives during outages.

questions.q: Why should organizations avoid using the cloud root or master account for daily operations?
choices: It holds unrestricted privileges and should be reserved and tightly protected
It is billed at a higher rate than other accounts
It cannot be assigned multi-factor authentication
It is automatically deleted after 90 days
questions.why: The root account has full control, so it should be locked down with MFA and used only for tasks requiring it, not routine work.

questions.q: What does 'ephemeral' compute (such as containers or functions) imply for logging?
choices: Logs persist automatically forever
Logs must be shipped off the instance before it is destroyed
Ephemeral workloads never need monitoring
Logging is impossible for short-lived workloads
questions.why: Short-lived resources vanish quickly, so telemetry and logs must be centralized externally to preserve audit and forensic value.

questions.q: In cloud, what is the main risk associated with overly permissive storage bucket policies?
choices: Unintended public exposure of sensitive data
Increased latency for authorized users
Loss of provider SLA credits
Automatic key rotation failures
questions.why: Misconfigured public buckets are a common cause of cloud data breaches, so access should default to private and least privilege.

questions.q: Which CSA-recommended control helps detect anomalous privileged activity in cloud accounts?
choices: Centralized logging with monitoring and alerting on management plane events
Removing MFA from privileged accounts
Disabling all audit trails to reduce noise
Sharing admin credentials to simplify tracking
questions.why: Aggregating and monitoring management plane logs enables detection of unusual privileged actions and rapid response.

questions.q: What is the primary advantage of infrastructure as code (IaC) for cloud security?
choices: Configurations are version-controlled, reviewable, and repeatable
It disables the management plane
It guarantees the provider assumes all risk
It removes the need for any access controls
questions.why: IaC makes infrastructure declarative and auditable, so security can be reviewed, tested, and enforced before deployment.

questions.q: Why is 'right to audit' language important in a cloud contract?
choices: It waives all provider liability
It replaces the need for encryption
It defines the customer's ability to verify provider security controls
It grants the provider access to customer data
questions.why: Right-to-audit clauses, or acceptable substitutes like third-party reports, let customers gain assurance over provider controls.

questions.q: In cloud IAM, what is the benefit of using temporary, scoped credentials for workloads?
choices: They eliminate the need for authorization policies
They grant permanent administrator access
They make logging unnecessary
They reduce the risk from long-lived static keys if exposed
questions.why: Short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials limit the window and scope of misuse compared to static long-lived keys.

questions.q: What does ENISA identify as a risk from shared technology and multi-tenancy?
choices: Isolation failure allowing one tenant to affect another
Automatic compliance with GDPR
Elimination of insider threats
Guaranteed performance for every tenant
questions.why: ENISA cites isolation failure, where a flaw in shared components lets one tenant impact or access another, as a key cloud risk.

questions.q: Which approach best addresses secrets management in cloud applications?
choices: Emailing keys to developers as needed
Embedding secrets in container image layers
Hardcoding credentials in source code repositories
Storing secrets in a dedicated vault and injecting them at runtime
questions.why: Dedicated secrets managers or vaults centralize, rotate, and control access to credentials rather than exposing them in code.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the CSA Security Guidance document?
choices: To certify individual cloud providers annually
To scan customer workloads for vulnerabilities
To serve as a legally binding regulation
To provide foundational best practices across cloud security domains
questions.why: The CSA Security Guidance organizes cloud security best practices into domains and is a core source for the CCSK exam.

questions.q: Why should encryption of data in transit be enforced even within a provider's network?
choices: Because provider networks are never trusted by regulation
To protect against interception on shared and internal network paths
Because it is required to create a VPC
To reduce storage costs
questions.why: Assuming zero trust, traffic can traverse shared segments, so TLS or equivalent protects confidentiality and integrity in transit.

questions.q: In cloud incident response, what is the value of pre-establishing provider contacts and escalation paths?
choices: It transfers legal liability to the provider
It reduces delay when coordinating response for provider-controlled layers
It automatically preserves all forensic evidence
It removes the need for an internal IR team
questions.why: Knowing who to contact and how to escalate at the provider speeds coordination during incidents involving shared responsibility.

questions.q: What distinguishes STAR Level 2 from STAR Level 1 in the CSA registry?
choices: Level 2 is a self-assessment while Level 1 is audited
Level 2 adds independent third-party assessment or certification
Level 2 is only for government agencies
Level 2 removes the need to complete the CCM
questions.why: STAR Level 2 builds on Level 1 by requiring third-party attestation or certification such as STAR Certification or Attestation.

questions.q: Why is 'zero trust' architecture increasingly recommended for cloud environments?
choices: It verifies every request regardless of network location instead of trusting the perimeter
It assumes internal traffic is always safe
It eliminates the need for identity verification
It relies solely on firewalls at the network edge
questions.why: Zero trust removes implicit network trust and continuously authenticates and authorizes each request, fitting distributed cloud.

questions.q: In a SaaS deployment, which security responsibility still typically remains with the customer?
choices: Securing the physical data center
Maintaining the hypervisor and host OS
Patching the underlying application code
Managing user access, identities, and data classification
questions.why: Even in SaaS the customer retains responsibility for identity, access management, and how its data is used and classified.
